newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Banking sector drives Moroccan bourse index lower.
newsitem.headline: Banking sector drives Moroccan bourse index lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended the week on Friday lower, driven down by banking sector stocks, including Banque Commerciale du Maroc, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index dropped 0.35 percent to 428.60 points compared with last Friday.

"After a short period of stagnation, the market index dropped slightly this week pulled down mainly by the banking stocks," Fatima Zohra Wahidi at Upline Securities said. But analysts expect the market to gain momentum soon after the listed companies started to publish their half-year results.
Wafabank, one maket blue chip, lost four dirhams to close at 505 dirhams compared with last week.
Wafabank, announced a net profit of 83 million dirhams ($9.5 million) for the first half of the year, up from 78.4 million dirhams in the same period last year.

Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, lost 30 dirhams in one week to close at 670 dirhams. Banc Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the most liquid stocks, lost 11 dirhams to close at 405 dirhams. It made a net profit of 259.3 million dirhams in the first half of 1996.

The bank, reporting on operations for Morocco, its Paris agency and Tanger free zone, said deposits rose in the first half of 1996 to 23.3 billion dirhams against 21.9 billion, giving it 14.3 percent of the market against 12.4 percent.

Earlier in 1996, the bank increased its capital to 443 million dirhams, through incorporation of reserves, a share distribution of two new shares for each seven old ones, and a $60 million international issue of Global Depository Receipts.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, lost 10 dirhams to close at 330 dirhams.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant and in which the government expects to sell up to 51 percent stake to foreign oil investors, dropped one dirham to close at 250 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which has interests in more than 40 companies, also lost five dirhams to close at 595 dirhams.
The traded volume on the official market was 45.8 million dirhams, up from 23.8 million dirhams compared with last week, stockbrokers said. ($1= 8.7 dirhams)
